Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this task changes a multi-wake dogfish target policy; I’ll follow its required keyframe inspection before proposing the single candidate. I’ll first read the workspace contract, then the skill instructions and rollout evidence.

The workspace has four sampled rollouts, all ending by left-domain exit; the current parent is the `e664…` prefill and the best sampled score is `0ab6…` at −11.1487. I’m now anchoring the keyframes to the written observations, metrics, inherited optimizer notes, and exact controller differences before making any edit.

The inherited logs close the obvious local knobs: rearward-bearing interpolation, added turn damping, and conditional overspeed damping all preserve the same upper-return failure. The only sampled structural discriminator (deep rearward plus simultaneous current/windowed opening) gives a small but consistent gain over its exact `−0.125` baseline, so I’m inspecting whether the keyframes support that as real delayed recovery or merely the same exit shifted slightly.

The keyframes show active upstream motion, not passive advection: mean fish x-velocity is about −0.071 to −0.074 versus local flow −0.048 to −0.051. But every candidate turns nose-up well before the target or developed cylinder wakes, then exits the upper boundary. I’m recording the candidate hypothesis now, as required by the visual-inspection skill, before touching the controller.

The selected candidate keeps the sampled approach controller and its strict recovery gate, changing only the gated terminal anterior allocation from partial unloading (`0.10`) to neutral (`0.0`). This follows the one mechanism with a controlled positive comparison; the durable lesson will explicitly bound that gain because the sampled rollout still never entered the wake corridor.

Both required provenance files now contain substantive evidence-backed changes. Per the workspace contract, I’m invoking the mandated checker in its three separate non-CFD stages: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract/schema, and editable-boundary validation.

The first checker exposed a rendered-workspace inconsistency before evaluating our changes: `README.md` lists the same assigned parent twice, so the checker counts two “copied to guidance” entries even though both are the identical optimizer ID. I’m inspecting the checker’s parent-resolution logic and will make the smallest in-workspace metadata repair needed, without touching solver or evaluation code.

The guidance check now passes after removing the duplicate identical parent entry. The Julia stage is currently blocked by the environment (`julia: command not found`), not by a policy assertion; I’m checking standard local tool locations and will still run the independent schema/static guard if no Julia binary is present.

All mandated checks are now passing: guidance/provenance semantics, Julia contract execution, and solver editable boundary. I found the bundled Julia runtime after the shell lacked it on `PATH`. I’m doing a final read-only audit of the exact candidate delta, parameter ownership, and required-file contents; no CFD rollout will be run.

Completed exactly one multi-wake candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): retains the best sampled approach and dual-opening terminal gate, strengthening only gated anterior unloading from `0.10` to `0.0`.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): visual diagnosis, evidence comparison, hypothesis, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:106): materially revised reusable lesson bounding the weak positive evidence for conjunctive terminal gating.
- Removed a duplicated identical assigned-parent entry from `README.md` so the required checker could resolve one parent.

Checks passed: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract/schema, and editable boundary. No CFD was run.
